title: Christie's New York to offer costumes and more from The Devil Wears Prada 2 in online auction
summary: Christie's global auction house will host a groundbreaking online auction featuring apparel and accessories from the hit 20th Century Studios film The Devil Wears Prada 2. The online auction will take place at christies.com from September 1 to September 15, with sales benefitting the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) and the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA). A free, public exhibition of the items being offered will take place at Christie's New York at 20 Rockefeller Plaza from September 8 to September 13, alongside the exhibition for Handbags Online: The September Edit. The online auction—conceived of and supported by The Devil Wears Prada 2 star Meryl Streep, who led efforts around a charity auction of costumes after the first film—will include many fashion pieces connected to the film, some worn by The Devil Wears Prada 2 stars Streep, Anne Hathaway, Emily Blunt, Stanley Tucci, Simone Ashley, and Lady Gaga on screen. title: Christopher Wierling and Simon Würsten Marin join Migros Museum curatorial team
summary: Migros Museum für Gegenwartskunst is strengthening its curatorial team with two new appointments: Christopher Wierling joins the museum in the newly established role of Curator of Exhibitions, while Simon Würsten Marin takes on the position of Curator of Programmes as a parental leave replacement. Bringing different experiences and perspectives, both will expand the museum's curatorial profile and contribute to the further development of its exhibitions and public programmes. Christopher Wierling joins the museum from Gropius Bau, Berlin, and will contribute his extensive institutional experience to the conceptual and structural development of the museum's exhibition formats. In particular, he will work closely with artists on the development and production of new works, while initiating and curating a range of exhibition projects. title: FOTOHOF presents Mafalda Rakoš exhibition It's Yours, It's Mine
summary: With »It’s Yours, It’s Mine: Seven Relational Portraits«, FOTOHOF presents an insight into the work of Austrian photographer Mafalda Rakoš. At the core of her projects—most of which unfold over extended periods of time—are questions that emerge from a mode of looking at the world that is at once photographically documentary and anthropologically investigative. Portraiture serves as the recurring aesthetic and medial point of departure for artistic experiments that explore the potential of photography to engage with complex social discourses. In Rakoš’s work, the image of the Other emerges through an expanded perspective. In dialogue with her protagonists and co-authors, she transcends the literary, scholarly, and artistic tradition of the first-person narrative. title: Mariana Cordoba's "Just Let Yourself Feel" at La Cometa Gallery in Miami
summary: In her most commanding work to date, the Colombian-American painter Mariana Cordoba renders emotion as architecture, building psychological space through gesture, color, and the eloquent logic of accumulation. There are paintings that reward interpretation, and paintings that resist it — not out of opacity, but out of a more radical demand. Just Let Yourself Feel, Cordoba's large scale painting on view at La Cometa Gallery in Miami’s Wynwood Arts District, belongs to the second category. This is not a work to be solved. It is a work to be inhabited. At first encounter, the canvas presents itself as pure chromatic event: electric blues cascade alongside acidic greens and pulsing yellows in what might, at an uninformed glance, be dismissed as gestural excess. title: Heritage Auctions to offer exceedingly rare meteorites, fossils and Manhattan Project glass
summary: Unmatched in its size, composition and presentation, a Seymchan Meteorite Sphere, weighing an astonishing 26.76 kilograms (59 pounds), could become the most coveted item of any meteorite collection after it crosses the auction block in Heritage's August 26 Natural History Signature® Auction, which will showcase some of the most exceptional specimens from the natural world, including many prized meteorite specimens. "This auction features some singular and truly exceptional specimens, including an immense Seymchan pallasite sphere, the main mass of the Stardust Mine Martian Meteorite, a 99-troy ounce gold nugget and massive slice of the Fukang Meteorite," says Craig Kissick, Vice President of Natural History for Heritage Auctions "The museum quality of these pieces makes me very proud to be in a position to offer them." title: Franklin Parrasch Gallery now representing Claire Colette
summary: Claire Colette’s meticulously rendered reductive compositions invite deep, meditative observation and a perceptual exploration of cosmic and natural phenomena. Systems in nature, boundaries, deep time, and universal order are recurring themes throughout the artist’s work as she investigates ritual, symbol, and sentience. Colette builds the surfaces of her paintings utilizing variations of acrylic, ash, salt, resin, and dried flowers that are later overlayed with thin washes of muted hues. Her palette is reflective of dusk, night, or dawn as she creates a refined geometric language to depict mental and emotional landscapes and expanded states or planes of consciousness. Claire Colette (b. 1980, Reims, France) received her MFA from Mills College, Oakland, CA (2013), and her BFA from the Art Institute of California – Los Angeles, Los Angeles, CA (2003). title: Disney legend Joe Ranft Family Archive leads Heritage's Art of Disney Auction
summary: Never-before-seen storyboards from Tim Burton’s The Nightmare Before Christmas, hand-colored Toy Story storyboards, original Monsters, Inc. artwork and deeply personal career artifacts from the family archive of Disney Legend Joe Ranft will make their public debut when Heritage Auctions presents The Art of Disney Signature® Auction, Aug. 21–23. The three-day event features more than 1,300 lots spanning nearly a century of Disney artistry, but its emotional centerpiece is the extraordinary late Joe Ranft Family Archive. Comprising more than 100 fresh-to-market works and personal artifacts, the archive chronicles the remarkable career of one of animation’s most influential storytellers—from his early days at Walt Disney Studios and Skellington Productions to his pivotal role as a member of Pixar’s legendary Brain Trust. title: UMBC gallery presents Lewis Hine exhibition focusing on Maryland child labor
summary: UMBC’s Albin O. Kuhn Library Gallery announces the exhibition Lewis Hine in Maryland, accompanied by Lisa Oppenheim/Lewis Hine: Spine/Verso, on view from August 24 through December 18. From 1908 to 1924, documentary photographer Lewis Hine (American, 1874–1940) traveled throughout the United States, using his camera to document child labor on behalf of the National Child Labor Committee (NCLC). He photographed children working in coal mines, cotton mills, farms, tenements, and city streets. The NCLC used Hine’s photographs and eyewitness reports to support its campaigns for labor regulation and reform. His images appeared in pamphlets, posters, traveling exhibitions, and lantern-slide presentations across the country. title: Sean Kelly presents Luke Agada's first solo exhibition with the gallery
summary: Sean Kelly will present When the Center Holds, Nigerian artist Luke Agada's first solo exhibition with the gallery. Bringing together a new body of paintings and drawings, the exhibition explores how meaning and belonging persist during periods of profound historical and cultural transformation. There will be an opening reception on Thursday, September 10, from 6–8pm. Agada's practice investigates the changing nature of contemporary identity through the lens of globalization, migration, and postcolonial thought. His enigmatic compositions feature incorporeal figures, fragmented architectures, and biomorphic forms that inhabit dreamlike landscapes untethered to a fixed geography. Existing between memory and imagination, these hybrid forms embody identities continually shaped through movement across histories, cultures, and systems of power. title: Sharing the National Collection: Hermannsburg Potters bring Central Desert ceramics to Temora
summary: A powerful group of First Nations works of art will be loaned to Temora Arts Centre in the Riverina region of New South Wales for two years as part of the Albanese Government’s Sharing the National Collection program. On display from 14 August, the loans feature works by the Hermannsburg Potters, a collective of Western Arrarnta artists from Central Australia. The Ntaria/Hermannsburg Potters from the Northern Territory are known for their vibrant handmade ceramic pots that encompass collective and individually lived histories on Country. The Temora Art Centre will display works by seven different women artists from Ntaria/Hermannsburg. These dynamic and colourful ceramics showcase the evolution of the artists’ practice over three decades. title: Poland Pavilion at Gwangju Biennale 2026 presents Rites of Passage
summary: What happens when one chapter of life has come to an end, but the next has yet to begin? Rites of Passage, an exhibition organised by the Adam Mickiewicz Institute for the Poland Pavilion at Gwangju Biennale 2026, explores the experience of transition—both on a personal and a global scale. The exhibition is curated by Paulina Olszewska and brings together artists from Poland and Korea: Alicja Bielawska, Urszula Broll, Inside Job (Ula Lucińska and Michał Knychaus), Park Saengkwang, Yeesookyung, and Anna Zaradny. Rites of Passage will be presented as part of the 16th Gwangju Biennale, held this year under the theme You Must Change Your Life. One of the most important contemporary art events in Asia, the Biennale will run from September 5 to November 15, 2026. title: 80WSE exhibition examines historic 1970 People's Flag Show
summary: 80WSE presents Incendiaries: The People's Flag Show 1970, examining the landmark exhibition at Judson Memorial Church and the networks of artists, activists, and communities that shaped it into a defining moment of art and cultural protest in the United States. Organized in collaboration with NYU's Fales Library & Special Collections and in cooperation with Judson Memorial Church, Incendiaries draws on rare photographs, video documentation, and archival materials from the Judson Memorial Church Archive to trace a formative chapter in the intertwined histories of art, activism, and public dissent. title: New Museum exhibition traces 400 years of cultural history on the Bowery
summary: The Bowery: Devil’s Mile is the first exhibition to trace the rich cultural history of New York’s oldest thoroughfare, illuminating the Bowery—now home to the New Museum—as one of the most infamous yet astonishingly underexplored streets in the world. Known in the twentieth century as a notorious skid row, the Bowery has had many incarnations: a Lenape footpath; a home to farms and cattle drives; the site of racetracks and pleasure gardens; a center of popular entertainment with theaters, concert halls, tattoo parlors, and dime museums; and most recently, the spine of a thriving artist community. This exhibition is an introduction to the richness and complexity of the Bowery and its generative power and concentrated energy as a street, a neighborhood, and a state of mind. title: Major Raimonds Staprāns retrospective to open at Latvian National Museum of Art
summary: Marking the centenary of the outstanding Latvian émigré artist, playwright and painter Raimonds Staprāns, the Latvian National Museum of Art presents the exhibition Raimonds Staprāns. The Architecture of Silence from 14 August 2026 to 17 January 2027 in the museum’s 4th-floor galleries. The centenary exhibition of Raimonds Staprāns (1926–2026) aims to introduce works never seen before in Latvia while providing a focused yet comprehensive overview of the artist’s career – from his earliest paintings of the 1950s to the last ones created in the 21st century. In the spring of 2025, the exhibition curator, Dr. art. Elita Ansone, had the opportunity to select paintings for the exhibition at the Latvian National Museum of Art directly from the artist’s studio in San Francisco. title: MoCA\CT announces a new exhibition: Connecticut Industry
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art Connecticut announces the opening of Michael Borders: Connecticut Industry, an expansive exhibition centered on the Connecticut-based artist’s monumental, multi-panel mural exploring the state’s history, landscape, industries, and communities. Part of the larger Looking for History exhibition, Borders’ show is on view from Thursday, August 13, until Sunday, November 15, 2026. Composed of eight painted panels, each measuring five by ten feet, Connecticut Industry Mural offers a sweeping visual portrait of the state’s eight counties. Read from bottom to top, the mural unfolds as a layered narrative of Connecticut’s development—from early Indigenous presence and colonial settlement to industrial expansion and the technological ingenuity that transformed the state. title: First major museum retrospective explores the legacy of pioneering ceramic artist Doyle Lane
summary: “Doyle Lane: Master of Clay,” the first major museum retrospective devoted to Los Angeles ceramic artist Doyle Lane (1923–2002), opens at The Huntington on Sept. 13, 2026, and remains on view through Feb. 22, 2027. Featuring works that range from intimate vessels to large-scale architectural commissions, the exhibition examines how Lane expanded the possibilities of ceramics in mid-20th-century California. Featuring more than 100 works from the 1950s through the 1980s, the exhibition offers the most expansive presentation to date of Lane’s practice, highlighting his technical command with glazes, including his mastery of difficult red tones that shift subtly from orange to deep crimson, often edged in black from the firing process. title: Contemporary works on paper exhibition opening at Newfields
summary: Rise Through Everything: Geometry, Rhythm, and Gesture unites visionary modern and contemporary Black artists who have transformed art on paper to cite cultural knowledge, express lived experiences, and engage in radical acts of self-definition. This exhibition, curated by Associate Curator of Works on Paper, Anna Stein, features 16 prints, photographs, drawings, and collages, including works from Yashua Klos, Derrick Adams and Ayana Jackson. “Perhaps my favorite thing about this exhibition is how many stunning additions to our collection it debuts,” said Stein. “Ten of the works are new acquisitions that really showcase the direction we are taking at Newfields with the experiences we are crafting and stories we are telling.” Placing newer voices alongside established masters, Rise Through Everything creates a dialogue

title: Brendan Fernandes explores sound and abstraction in new exhibition The Noise Will Sound
summary: The Noise Will Sound presents a new body of work by Brendan Fernandes that considers the relationship between sound, visibility, and abstraction. Through layered textiles, fragmented figures, and richly textured surfaces, the exhibition explores how noise can exist beyond the audible, emerging instead as something visual, embodied, and deeply felt. For Fernandes, noise is both a formal and political condition. It prompts questions about who is heard, who is overlooked, and who determines the difference between signal and disruption. Within his new series of photographic works shot on film titled Noise See, fragmented bodies dissolve into patterned compositions, creating moments of visual dissonance that challenge perception and invite sustained looking. The photographs ask viewers to consider not only what they see, but what they imagine

title: Galerie Ron Mandos presents Zanele Muholi exhibition Hlanganani
summary: Galerie Ron Mandos will present Hlanganani (“Bring Together”), a new exhibition by South African visual activist Prof. Sir Zanele Muholi, opening Saturday 12 September 2026. Presented together with the Muholi Art Institute, the exhibition marks twenty years since Muholi began Faces and Phases and brings together new self-portraits, recent work, and a new body of Faces and Phases portraits made with Amsterdam’s Black queer community. On view through Saturday, 1 November 2026. Zanele Muholi (b. 1972, Umlazi, Durban) is an internationally recognised visual activist and photographer, known for a body of work that documents and celebrates the lives of South Africa’s Black lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer and intersex communities. summary: untame flow stay release is an exhibition and research presentation curated by Jussi Koitela and Aneta Rostkowska at Temporary Gallery in Cologne. It features work by Ren Loren Britton, Justyna Górowska, Anke Haller, Pia Lindman, Finnegan Shannon, Cecilia Vicuña and Jenni-Juulia Wallinheimo-Heimonen, alongside a research presentation. The exhibition architecture is by Jakob Engel.
